content: Didanosine, whether used alone or in combination with other medications, has the potential to cause severe damage to the liver and pancreas, as well as a condition known as lactic acidosis. Inform your doctor if you currently consume or have previously consumed large amounts of alcohol, if you use or have used street drugs, or if you have a history of Crohn's disease, cystic fibrosis, diabetes, high cholesterol, or liver or pancreatic disease. Additionally, notify your doctor and pharmacist if you are taking stavudine (Zerit), especially if you are pregnant. It is crucial to inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are currently taking or have taken any of the following medications: acetaminophen (Tylenol, others); allopurinol (Zyloprim); amiodarone (Cordarone, Pacerone); azathioprine (Imuran); cholesterol-lowering medications (statins); dantrolene (Dantrium); furosemide (Lasix); hormone replacement therapy; iron products; isoniazid (INH, Nydrazid); ketoconazole (Nizoral); medications for HIV or AIDS; 6-mercaptopurine (Purinethol); methotrexate (Rheumatrex); methyldopa (Aldoril); niacin (nicotinic acid); oral contraceptives (birth control pills); oral steroids such as dexamethasone (Decadron, Dexone), methylprednisolone (Medrol), and prednisone (Deltasone); pentamidine (Nebupent, Pentam); piroxicam (Feldene); pyrazinamide (Rifater); ribavirin (Rebetron); rifampin (Rifadin, Rimactane); salicylate pain relievers such as aspirin, choline magnesium trisalicylate (Trisalicylate), choline salicylate (Arthropan), diflunisal (Dolobid), magnesium salicylate (Doan's, others), and salsalate (Argesic, Disalcid, Salsalate); sulfonamide antibiotics such as sulfadiazine, sulfamethizole (Urobiotic), sulfasalazine (Azulfidine), and sulfisoxazole (Eryzole, Gantrisin, Pediazole); sulindac (Clinoril); valproic acid (Depakene, Depakote); or products containing kava. If you experience any of the following symptoms, contact your doctor immediately: nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, abdominal pain or swelling, severe back pain, extreme fatigue, weakness, dizziness, lightheadedness, rapid heartbeat, sudden onset of a slow or irregular heartbeat, deep or rapid breathing, shortness of breath, dark yellow or brown urine, unusual bleeding or bruising, yellowing of the skin or eyes, feeling cold, fever, or flu-like symptoms. Discuss with your doctor the safe use of alcohol while taking didanosine, as alcohol consumption can increase the risk of serious side effects. Ensure you attend all scheduled appointments with your doctor and laboratory, as specific tests will be ordered to monitor your body's response to didanosine. Speak with your doctor about the risks associated with taking this medication. Didanosine is prescribed in combination with other medications to treat human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection in patients with or without acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS). It belongs to a class of medications called nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NRTIs) and works by slowing the spread of HIV in the body. However, didanosine does not cure HIV infection, prevent the development of HIV-related illnesses, or stop the transmission of HIV to others. Didanosine is available as extended-release capsules, chewable tablets, powder for oral solution, and liquid solution, all of which are taken orally. It is typically taken once or twice daily on an empty stomach, either 30 minutes before or 2 hours after eating. To ensure consistent dosing, take it at the same time(s) each day. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take didanosine exactly as directed, without altering the dose or frequency. If using extended-release capsules, swallow them whole without splitting, chewing, crushing, or opening them. Chewable tablets should be chewed thoroughly or dissolved in at least 1 ounce of water before swallowing. You may add 1 ounce (2 tablespoons) of clear apple juice to the mixture for flavor, but do not use other types of juice. Drink the liquid immediately. If using the powder form, mix it with water just before taking it. Dissolve the powder in 4 ounces (1/2 cup) of water, stir for 2–3 minutes until fully dissolved, and drink immediately. Do not mix the powder with fruit juice or other liquids. If using the liquid solution, shake it well before each use and measure the dose with a proper measuring spoon or cup, not a household spoon. Continue taking didanosine even if you feel well, as it controls HIV infection but does not cure it. Do not stop taking it without consulting your doctor, as missed doses or discontinuation may make your condition harder to treat. Didanosine may also be used with another medication to help prevent HIV infection in healthcare workers or others accidentally exposed to the virus. Discuss the potential risks of using this drug for your condition with your doctor. It may also be prescribed for other uses; consult your doctor or pharmacist for more information. Before taking didanosine, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to didanosine, aspartame (NutraSweet), antacids, or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, and nutritional supplements you are taking, especially those mentioned in the Important Warning section. Some medications must be taken several hours before or after didanosine; consult your doctor for specific timing instructions. Notify your doctor if you are on a low-salt diet or have a history of eye disease, vision problems, muscle issues, gout, peripheral neuropathy, radiation therapy, phenylketonuria (PKU), or heart or kidney disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking didanosine, contact your doctor immediately. Do not breastfeed if you are HIV-positive or taking didanosine. Be aware that didanosine may cause side effects requiring immediate treatment, especially in children who may not be able to communicate their symptoms. Ask your child's doctor how to recognize these side effects. Additionally, didanosine may cause changes in body fat distribution, such as increased fat in the breasts or upper back. Unless otherwise directed by your doctor, continue your normal diet. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Minor side effects of didanosine include diarrhea, headache, and muscle pain. Notify your doctor if these symptoms are severe or persistent. Serious side effects, though uncommon, include hives, skin rash, itching, difficulty breathing or swallowing, numbness or tingling in the hands or feet, blurred vision, difficulty distinguishing colors, and chills. Contact your doctor immediately if you experience any of these symptoms or those listed in the Important Warning section. Store didanosine capsules, tablets, and powder in their original containers, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep them at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture. Use mixtures of tablets and apple juice within 1 hour and mixtures of powder and water within 4 hours. Refrigerate liquid didanosine, keep it tightly closed, and discard any unused medication after 30 days. Dispose of expired or unneeded medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call 911. Symptoms of overdose may include diarrhea, numbness or tingling in the hands or feet, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, abdominal pain or swelling, severe back pain, extreme fatigue, weakness, dizziness, lightheadedness, rapid or irregular heartbeat, deep or rapid breathing, shortness of breath, dark yellow or brown urine, unusual bleeding or bruising, yellowing of the skin or eyes, feeling cold, fever, or flu-like symptoms. Do not share your medication with others. Consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription. If you spill didanosine powder or liquid, clean the area with a wet mop or damp sponge using soap and water. Avoid creating airborne dust, and wash your hands and cleaning materials thoroughly after use.
